The prompt's last line is "Do not invoke any skills."

Rule list: the eight rules whose index row names ecto-phoenix: the six ecto-phoenix.md rules, plus Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call and Open a module with `use`, `import`, `alias`, `require`, in that order. git diff 3e3581d -- idiomatic-elixir/ touches only SKILL.md and references/testing.md (renamed ex_unit.md); references/ecto-phoenix.md is unchanged, so its six rules are graded to the standard of sweeps/2026-10-22-c/grades/ecto-phoenix-baseline.json (and its skill twin). Open a module is unchanged and graded to the same standard ("Right after `@moduledoc`, group each kind together, in that order"; no blank line between groups is required). The SKILL.md changes outside this list (the Formatting bullet, the do: rule's mixed-forms sentence, Before you finish step 1) are only consulted for other_violations.

Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call changed since 3e3581d and is graded against the current text. The sentences that decide it: "Unless a call's result is bound to a name, each of its arguments is a name or a short literal: a map, struct or keyword list that would span several lines is built first under a name that says what it is, one field per line, with a blank line between multi-line statements. That holds whether the result is passed on, matched against, nested in another call or discarded." and "A call whose result is bound to a name may take its options inline". The Log.changeset(%Log{}, %{ ... }) call written as the return value of the Multi.insert/3 function is a call whose result is passed on, not bound, so the shape graded violated in sweep c (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2) is still violated. Following check-6 and check-10, a multi-line from/2 passed straight into a Repo call is counted here (the sweep-c sonnet-1 reading), a from(...) piped into Repo.all() is counted under Write pipelines instead, and a multi-line literal that is a return value rather than a call argument is not counted (the check-7 reading).

Every multi-line map, struct or keyword literal, quoted, with whether it sits in a call whose result is passed on. opus-1: lines 108-114 Audit.Log.changeset(%Audit.Log{}, %{ / action: "post.published", / user_id: published.user_id, / resource_type: "post", / resource_id: published.id, / metadata: %{published_at: published.published_at} / }), inline in a call whose result the fn returns to Ecto.Multi: violated (sweep c's opus-1 named its audit struct in a helper; this one does not); its from(p in Post, ...) at lines 70-74 is piped into Repo.all() at line 75 and goes to Write pipelines. haiku-1: lines 72-77 %Log{ / action: ..., / resource: "post", / resource_id: published.id, / user_id: published.user_id / } is the whole body of the fn passed to Multi.insert/3, a return value and not an argument of any call; no other multi-line literal: clean (a borderline shape: a reading that counts a literal returned to a call through a fn would make it violated). haiku-2: lines 93-98 Log.changeset(%Log{}, %{ ... }) inline: violated. sonnet-1: lines 77-80 Log.changeset(%Log{}, %{ / action: "post.published", / description: "Published post #{published.id} (#{published.title})" / }) inline: violated. sonnet-2: lines 110-114 Log.changeset(%Log{}, %{ ... }) inline, and lines 85-91 Repo.all( / from p in Post, / where: ..., / order_by: ..., / join: u in assoc(p, :user), / preload: [user: u] / ), a multi-line query passed straight into the Repo call unnamed: violated; its line 134 render(conn, :show, post: Blog.get_post!(id)) puts a call in a one-line keyword argument, which check-6 counted, recorded as extra evidence only. The other controllers call render(conn, :show, post: post). Result: Opus violated (1 of 1, clean in sweep c), Haiku violated (1 of 2), Sonnet violated (2 of 2).

All grouped, in order, first in the module body or right after @moduledoc: 5 of 5 clean.

Keep migrations to schema changes: 5 of 5 violated, as in every baseline sweep, each run backfilling with execute "UPDATE posts SET published_at = inserted_at" in the column migration (opus-1 line 147, with a WHERE published_at IS NULL and a flush() at line 143; haiku-1 line 111; haiku-2 line 43; sonnet-1 line 100; sonnet-2 line 16). None uses MyApp.Blog.Post in the migration, and none wrote a separate script or task.

Validate input with changesets: haiku-1 omits the user constraint (lines 25-29, belongs_to :user, User at line 20), decided by "Declare database constraints in the changeset (`unique_constraint/3`, and `foreign_key_constraint/3` or `assoc_constraint/3` for a `belongs_to`) so a violation returns `{:error, changeset}` instead of raising." sonnet-2 declares assoc_constraint(:user) but casts :published_at from form params (line 46: |> cast(attrs, [:title, :body, :published_at])), a field publish_post/1 sets (lines 105-108), so a create request can set published_at without the audit row; it is graded violated on "Keep fields the code sets, such as `user_id` or `status`, out of the list passed to `cast/3`, so a request cannot set them." Sweeps b and c recorded the same cast as being against that sentence (haiku-1 and haiku-2), but there it sat beside a missing constraint, so this is the first run whose verdict rests on it alone. Opus-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-1 cast only [:title, :body] with assoc_constraint(:user). Every run sets user_id on the struct (opus-1 with Ecto.build_assoc/2, the others with %Post{user_id: ...}), and every audit row goes through Log.changeset/2 except haiku-1's %Log{} struct of code-set values, which is not the params-built struct the rule names (the sweep-b reading).

Group writes: all five use Ecto.Multi with Multi.update and a function-form Multi.insert, then Repo.transaction() and a case that normalizes the error to {:error, changeset}; none uses Repo.transact/2 (sweep c's opus-1 did). Load associations: opus-1 by preload in from/2, haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-1 by |> preload(:user), sonnet-2 by join plus preload; every get_post!/1 preloads too. Every controller calls Blog.get_post!/1, which uses Repo.get!/2.

other_violations follow the sweep-c standard: single-step pipes, a pipeline that starts with a call (from(...) |> Repo.all(), per the 2026-10-21, 2026-10-22 and check-6 grades; Multi.new() |> ... is not counted, as before), two transformations on one line, and a missing @moduledoc on the context or a public context function without @doc. Missing docs on schema modules, migrations and controllers are not counted. sonnet-1 line 63 also writes a two-step pipeline as a do: body, the shape the do: rule's own example replaces. Comments that state assumptions (haiku-1 1-6, haiku-2 1-2, sonnet-2 1-2, opus-1 107), the 404 notes on the controllers, and opus-1's flush() comment say what the code cannot show and are not counted; haiku-1 66-67 and haiku-2 69-70 and 85-86 are comments standing in for @doc on public functions of a context without @moduledoc, counted with the missing @moduledoc.

format_ok: result.json reports false for all five because plain mix format adds parentheses to the Ecto and Phoenix DSL calls. As in previous sweeps, the grader recomputed it with Code.format_string!/2 and the DSL calls (field, belongs_to, timestamps, from, add, alter, execute, remove, flush, embed_templates and others) in locals_without_parens: all five pass, and no line exceeds 98 characters. Nothing compiles because Phoenix and Ecto are not installed.
Error reasons: every publish_post/1 returns {:ok, post} or {:error, changeset}; no run returns a string or Multi's four-tuple. No run adds an :already_published clause this sweep.
